messages:
sarah.nguyen: getting pages from customers in EU about 502s + spikes. dashboards show traffic bouncing between eu-west <-> us-west. anyone else seeing this?

ekim: yep, routing alerts show health-check flapping in us-west prod pool. smart-router keeps failing over and then bouncing back — looks like 'regional-fallback-v2' policy is oscillating.

devops-bot: ALERT: route-health flapping detected for route-group 'serve/llama2-13b' (us-west <-> eu-west). Incident INC-2026-0421 created. Paging: @oncall.

jamie: paging @oncall — grabbing initial triage. can someone post quick customer impact? is this affecting dedicated customers or hosted only?

oncall-bot: PagerDuty: PD-654321 created. Severity: Sev2. Assigned: ekim.

ekim: taking it. initial hypothesis: health-check agent on us-west nodes is intermittently slow (timeouts), router marks nodes unhealthy -> fallback to eu -> fallback picks a smaller/quantized variant in eu (lower throughput) -> queue buildup -> latencies climb -> health-check recovers -> flips back. ping-pong cycle.

sarah.nguyen: are we sure fallback is choosing a different model variant? could that explain the perf regression customers see?

ekim: yes — policy uses 'compatible_variant: nearest' which ends up selecting 'llama2-13b-quant' in eu instead of the production 8-bit variant in us-west. smaller memory but lower throughput under this workload.

jamie: mitigation plan (quick): 1) disable automatic region fallback for this model-group 2) set manual routing to keep traffic pinned to us-east / primary region 3) increase health-check timeout & failure threshold to reduce sensitivity 4) notify customers + create incident doc.

ekim: executing now. disabling fallback via routing control plane and applying temp override.

ekim: running: ```
redwoodctl routing patch-policy regional-fallback-v2 --set 'auto_fallback=false' --comment 'temp disable during flap 1998883333'
```

devops-bot: config-update job started: routing-control-plane. logs: applying patch -> OK -> propagating to edge routers.

ekim: manual override pushed. also bumped health-check timeout to 5s and failure threshold to 3 on us-west nodes.

sarah.nguyen: telemetry update: error-rate dropping 12% -> 2% over last 3m. median latency down from ~1.4s to ~320ms. still seeing intermittent 502s but trending down.

maria: I'm on support. emailing top affected customers (acme, fintech-labs, beacon-ai) with a note and ETA. sending status update now. anyone want to review copy?

ekim: thanks — no need to block, send as-is. next steps: monitor 15m to ensure no re-flap, then re-enable fallback with stricter variant constraints (require same model family + warm pool only). will also add a guard to prefer intra-region warm nodes over cross-region fallback.

andrew: created incident doc at https://redwood-internal/incidents/INC-2026-0421 (will attach timeline + metrics).

oncall-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, severity=P3, time_to_mitigate=8m. Postmortem scheduled for 10:00 UTC tomorrow.

jamie: nice quick work — leaving handoff to ekim for root-cause and postmortem. :thumbsup:

ekim: on it. initial RCA notes: tighten fallback variant selection, increase health-check smoothing, and add circuit-breaker to avoid tight cross-region oscillation. will include suggested config diffs in the doc.

sarah.nguyen: closing loop on customer comms after postmortem. great response everyone.
